items.title: New Radicals Quietly Release First New Song In 28 Years
items.summary: Gregg Alexander ended New Radicals after their lone album, 1998's acclaimed Maybe You've Been Brainwashed Too, but went on to become one of pop's most successful behind-the-scenes songwriters. He co-wrote hits like Sophie Ellis-Bextor's "Murder On The Dancefloor," Santana and Michelle Branch's "The Game Of Love," and the Oscar-nominated Begin Again song "Lost Stars," recorded by Keira Knightley and Adam Levine.

items.title: Tori Amos Covers The Swell Season In Tribute To Glen Hansard
items.summary: Earlier this week, Glen Hansard tragically passed away in a motorcycle crash at the age of 56. Bono paid tribute to the Oscar-winning Irish singer-songwriter and actor with heartfelt words on social media. Last night, Tori Amos commemorated him with a cover of the Swell Season's "Falling Slowly" at Boston's Leader Bank Pavilion. items.title: Ed Askew Didn’t Want to Paint It Black
items.summary: Ed Askew’s first album, a 1968 self-titled release (later issued as Ask the Unicorn), on the ESP-Disk label, was almost his last.
